35.text:
Theatres, orchestras and museums often depend on grants, and some believe that the arts should be funded by government. I largely agree, since the market alone would neglect many valuable forms of art, although public money should be spent carefully and without political control.

To begin with, public funding allows the arts to exist where the market alone would neglect them. Commercial success rewards popular entertainment, so experimental theatre, classical music and local museums often need grants to survive and to offer low prices. A small theatre that stages new plays, for example, may never make a profit but enriches the cultural life of a city. Without subsidy, ticket prices would rise beyond the means of many people, and only the richest would enjoy the arts. Public support also protects cultural heritage, such as archives and traditional performances, which have no commercial value but great importance for national identity. Society gains cultural diversity and wider access to the arts.

Furthermore, the arts bring benefits that justify public spending. They attract tourists, create jobs, improve the quality of city life and contribute to education and wellbeing. Studies of many cities suggest that every unit of money spent on culture returns a larger amount in local spending. However, funding should be limited and fair. Money spent on the arts cannot be used for hospitals and schools, so priorities have to be balanced, and governments must not use funds to control content or to support only the art that they approve of. An independent arts council, which allocates grants through open competition, protects artistic freedom. Artists and companies should also be encouraged to earn some income themselves.

In conclusion, the arts should be funded by government to a large extent, because they enrich society and would otherwise suffer, provided that funding is independent and balanced with other needs.

Ví dụ nhà hát nhỏ dàn dựng vở mới có thể không bao giờ có lãi nhưng làm giàu đời sống văn hoá thành phố. 191.text:
Governments cannot fund everything, and opinions are divided as to whether public money should be spent mainly on science or on arts funding. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of science funding argue that science drives medicine, technology and economic growth. Research produces new treatments, cleaner energy, faster communication and discoveries that improve living standards for everyone. A single breakthrough, such as a vaccine, can save millions of lives and repay its cost many times over. Countries that invest heavily in research tend to have stronger economies and greater security, and young scientists need training, laboratories and long-term support that only governments can provide. Pressing problems, from disease to climate change, can be solved only through scientific knowledge.

On the other hand, supporters of arts funding point out that the arts develop creativity, identity and wellbeing. Museums, theatres and music give people a sense of belonging and meaning, bring communities together and attract visitors, and creative skills are increasingly valued in modern work. An engineer who designs a bridge, for example, needs science to make it strong and art to make it beautiful. Arts and science also support each other, since scientific thinking depends on imagination. Without funding, many cultural institutions would close, and future generations would be culturally poorer.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that science should receive the larger share, because it addresses urgent material needs and drives growth, but the arts deserve a stable and meaningful budget, since a society needs both prosperity and culture.

Khoa học thúc đẩy y học, công nghệ, tăng trưởng: nghiên cứu cho điều trị mới, năng lượng sạch, liên lạc nhanh; một đột phá như vaccine cứu hàng triệu người và hoàn vốn nhiều lần; nước đầu tư mạnh có kinh tế mạnh và an ninh; nhà khoa học trẻ cần đào tạo, phòng thí nghiệm và hỗ trợ dài hạn từ chính phủ; vấn đề cấp bách (bệnh, khí hậu) chỉ giải bằng khoa học.

Nghệ thuật phát triển sáng tạo, bản sắc, sức khoẻ tinh thần: bảo tàng, nhà hát, âm nhạc cho cảm giác thuộc về và ý nghĩa, gắn kết cộng đồng, thu hút khách; kỹ năng sáng tạo ngày càng được coi trọng. Ví dụ kỹ sư thiết kế cầu cần khoa học để cầu vững và nghệ thuật để đẹp. Khoa học cần trí tưởng tượng; không tài trợ nhiều tổ chức văn hoá đóng cửa.

251.text:
Cities and countries often have to choose between repairing old monuments and building new roads, bridges and railways, and opinions differ on whether public money should be spent on cultural heritage or on new infrastructure. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of heritage argue that it cannot be replaced. Historic buildings, traditions and sites carry the identity of a nation and attract visitors from around the world, and once lost they cannot be rebuilt. A medieval bridge that is allowed to fall into the river, for example, can never be rebuilt, whereas a modern road can be repaired next year. Heritage teaches people about their past, which helps them to understand who they are, and tourism linked to historic sites creates jobs and income for local people. Money spent on conservation is therefore an investment in something that belongs to future generations as well.

On the other hand, supporters of infrastructure point out that it meets daily needs. Roads, water supply, energy, hospitals and public transport affect safety, jobs and living standards immediately, and poor infrastructure can hold back whole regions. A town without reliable roads or clean water, for instance, will find it hard to care about its old buildings. In developing countries especially, basic services must come first, and there is a danger that heritage becomes a luxury when people lack essentials. Good infrastructure also helps tourists to reach heritage sites.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that a balanced budget is wise: urgent infrastructure should receive priority where people lack basic services, while irreplaceable heritage should be protected, as its loss would be permanent.

Di sản không thể thay thế: toà nhà, truyền thống, di tích mang bản sắc quốc gia, thu hút du khách và mất rồi không xây lại được. Ví dụ cây cầu trung cổ để rơi xuống sông không bao giờ xây lại, còn đường hiện đại sửa được năm sau. Dạy mọi người về quá khứ; du lịch gắn di tích tạo việc làm; chi bảo tồn là đầu tư cho thế hệ sau.

Đáp ứng nhu cầu hằng ngày: đường, nước, năng lượng, bệnh viện, giao thông công cộng ảnh hưởng an toàn, việc làm, mức sống ngay; hạ tầng kém kìm hãm cả vùng. Ngân sách cân bằng: hạ tầng khẩn cấp ưu tiên ở nơi thiếu, di sản không thể thay thế được bảo vệ.

322.text:
Films, books, music, theatre and design employ millions of people and shape national identity, and the question is how far governments should subsidise cultural industries. I believe that they should do so to a considerable extent, since subsidies can protect valuable local culture, although support must be targeted and time-limited where possible.

To begin with, subsidies can protect cultural industries from global competition. Small film, publishing and music sectors cannot match the budgets of international giants, and support lets local stories and languages survive while creating jobs and exports. A small country that funds its own films, for example, can tell stories in its own language that foreign studios would never produce. Without support, audiences might see little of their own culture, and young artists might leave to work abroad. Subsidies for training, festivals and translation also open international markets to local creators, so that cultural products become a source of pride and income.

Furthermore, cultural industries bring wider benefits. They create jobs, attract tourists, improve the image of a country and contribute to education and social cohesion. Some cultural activity, such as poetry, folk music or minority-language publishing, will never be commercially profitable, yet it has great value for society. However, too much aid can reduce efficiency. Producers who rely on guaranteed funding may take few risks or make work that appeals to officials instead of audiences, and taxpayers may question paying for entertainment that others enjoy. Support should therefore be competitive, transparent and linked to results, with some projects expected to earn part of their income. Money should be especially available for those that would otherwise disappear.

In conclusion, governments should subsidise cultural industries to a large extent, because they protect diversity and create wider benefits, provided that the support is targeted and accountable.

413.text:
Exchange programmes, festivals and cooperation projects between countries involve students, artists and professionals, and opinions differ on whether public money should go to cultural exchange or to infrastructure. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of cultural exchange argue that it builds understanding and brings long-term benefits. Young people who study or work in another country develop language skills, confidence and a wider outlook, and contact between peoples can reduce prejudice and strengthen friendships between nations. A student who spends a year abroad, for example, often returns with contacts that lead to trade, research or partnerships later in life. Cultural links also encourage tourism and trade, and they help a country's reputation. Such programmes are cheap compared with many infrastructure projects, and their effects may last for generations.

On the other hand, supporters of infrastructure point out that it meets urgent needs. Roads, railways, water supply and electricity affect daily life, jobs and growth, and a country that lacks them will struggle to benefit from any exchange. A farmer whose produce rots because there is no road to market, for instance, has more pressing needs than an exchange scholarship. Infrastructure projects also create employment and make a country attractive to investors, while the benefits of cultural programmes are harder to measure. In poor regions, basic services must take priority, because without them people cannot take advantage of educational and cultural opportunities.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that infrastructure should take priority where basic needs are unmet, but that modest and well-targeted exchange programmes represent excellent value and should not be neglected.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: chi cho chương trình trao đổi văn hoá hay hạ tầng

plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế (chương trình trao đổi, lễ hội, hợp tác liên quan sinh viên, nghệ sĩ, chuyên gia) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng hạ tầng ưu tiên khi thiếu nhu cầu cơ bản nhưng chương trình trao đổi nhỏ có mục tiêu rất đáng đồng tiền.

Xây hiểu biết và lợi ích dài hạn: người trẻ học hoặc làm việc nước khác phát triển ngôn ngữ, tự tin, tầm nhìn; giao lưu giảm định kiến, củng cố tình bạn giữa quốc gia. Ví dụ sinh viên một năm ở nước ngoài về nước với quan hệ dẫn đến thương mại, nghiên cứu, hợp tác về sau. Khuyến khích du lịch, thương mại; rẻ so với nhiều dự án hạ tầng; tác dụng qua nhiều thế hệ.

Đáp ứng nhu cầu cấp bách: đường, đường sắt, nước, điện ảnh hưởng đời sống, việc làm, tăng trưởng; nước thiếu hạ tầng khó hưởng lợi từ trao đổi. Ví dụ nông dân nông sản thối vì không có đường ra chợ có nhu cầu cấp bách hơn học bổng trao đổi. Dự án hạ tầng tạo việc làm, thu hút nhà đầu tư; lợi ích văn hoá khó đo; vùng nghèo dịch vụ cơ bản phải ưu tiên.
Hạ tầng ưu tiên khi nhu cầu cơ bản thiếu, nhưng chương trình trao đổi nhỏ có mục tiêu đáng đồng tiền.

473.text:
Governments are regularly asked to fund new galleries, theatres, stadiums and sports programmes, and opinions are divided as to whether public money should go to the arts or to sports development. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of sports development argue that sport improves health and brings communities together. Regular exercise reduces obesity and heart disease, saves health costs and gives young people a positive way to spend their time. Sporting success also creates national pride and provides role models, and major events attract visitors and publicity. A new public swimming pool in a poorer district, for example, can give hundreds of children a place to exercise that their families could not otherwise afford. Sport teaches teamwork, discipline and resilience, and it often draws in young people who are not interested in more traditional cultural activities.

On the other hand, supporters of the arts point out that they develop creativity, cultural identity and mental wellbeing. Museums, theatres and music give people meaning and a sense of belonging, bring communities together and attract tourists. Arts education improves concentration and confidence, and cultural industries create many jobs. Without public support, many cultural activities would disappear, as they cannot survive on commercial income alone, whereas professional sport, with its television rights and sponsors, is often able to fund itself. Culture also records and passes on the stories of a society.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Overall, I believe that a balanced budget is best, with sport funding concentrated on community and school facilities that improve public health, and arts funding directed to activities that the market would neglect.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: chi cho nghệ thuật hay phát triển thể thao

plan.think: Mở bài nêu thực tế (chính phủ thường được yêu cầu tài trợ phòng triển lãm, nhà hát, sân vận động, chương trình thể thao) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng cân bằng với thể thao tập trung cộng đồng, nghệ thuật cho hoạt động thị trường bỏ qua.

Thể thao cải thiện sức khoẻ, gắn kết cộng đồng: vận động giảm béo phì, bệnh tim, tiết kiệm chi phí y tế, cho người trẻ cách dùng thời gian tích cực; thành công thể thao tạo tự hào quốc gia, hình mẫu; sự kiện lớn thu hút khách. Ví dụ hồ bơi công mới ở khu nghèo. Dạy làm việc nhóm, kỷ luật, bền bỉ; thu hút người trẻ không thích hoạt động văn hoá truyền thống.

Nghệ thuật phát triển sáng tạo, bản sắc, sức khoẻ tinh thần: bảo tàng, nhà hát, nhạc cho ý nghĩa, cảm giác thuộc về, gắn kết, thu hút du khách; giáo dục nghệ thuật cải thiện tập trung và tự tin; công nghiệp văn hoá tạo việc làm. Không hỗ trợ công nhiều hoạt động biến mất vì không sống được bằng thu nhập thương mại, trong khi thể thao chuyên nghiệp có bản quyền truyền hình, nhà tài trợ thường tự lo; văn hoá ghi lại và truyền câu chuyện xã hội.
Ngân sách cân bằng: thể thao tập trung cơ sở cộng đồng và trường học cải thiện sức khoẻ; nghệ thuật cho hoạt động thị trường bỏ qua.

57.text:
Historic towns, ancient languages and traditional music are disappearing in many places, and some countries put considerable effort into protecting them. This essay will outline two principal benefits for a country that focuses on cultural preservation: economic gains and a stronger sense of identity.

First and foremost, cultural preservation brings economic benefits. Historic sites, festivals and traditions attract visitors who spend money on hotels, restaurants and souvenirs, and tourism based on heritage creates jobs for guides, craftspeople and hospitality workers. A well-preserved old town, for example, can draw visitors from around the world and support hundreds of local jobs. Heritage also gives communities a reason to maintain buildings and skills that might otherwise be lost, and it supports industries such as traditional crafts, local food and film locations. Italy, Egypt and Cambodia are examples of countries where cultural heritage is a major source of income.

In addition, cultural preservation strengthens identity, education and social cohesion. Historic sites, languages and traditions teach new generations about their roots and give communities a shared sense of belonging, which can help to bring together people of different backgrounds. Schools can use museums and monuments to bring history alive, and young people who understand their heritage are more likely to respect it. Preservation also protects knowledge that cannot be replaced, such as languages or craft techniques that, once lost, cannot be recreated. Although conservation can be expensive and may conflict with development, careful planning can protect the past while allowing the future to be built.

To sum up, cultural preservation brings clear benefits to a country, above all income from tourism and a stronger sense of identity. For these reasons, it deserves sustained public support.

Ví dụ phố cổ được bảo tồn tốt thu hút khách khắp thế giới và nuôi hàng trăm việc làm địa phương. 60.text:
In many schools, art and music lessons are the first to be cut when timetables are crowded, and some argue that they should be compulsory. I largely agree, since arts and music education develop creativity and confidence in every child, although the amount of compulsory time should be reasonable.

To begin with, arts and music education develops creativity, discipline and confidence in every child. Learning an instrument or practising drawing trains concentration and patience, gives children a way to express feelings and may reveal talents that would otherwise remain hidden. A shy pupil who joins the school choir, for example, may discover a talent and gain confidence that she would never have found in maths class. Research suggests that musical training is linked with better memory and language skills, and group performances teach teamwork and perseverance. Making these subjects compulsory also ensures access for pupils whose families cannot pay for private lessons or equipment, so that opportunities do not depend on income.

Furthermore, the arts prepare young people for working life and for life as citizens. Employers value creativity, communication and the ability to work with others, and cultural experiences help young people to understand different perspectives. However, compulsion has costs. The time required may reduce time for core subjects, and pupils who dislike a particular art form may feel forced. A sensible compromise would require a modest number of hours of arts and music each week, within which pupils can choose between drawing, drama, singing or instruments, while schools ensure that teaching is of good quality. Provided that lessons are enjoyable and well taught, compulsion can introduce many children to something they will value for life.

In conclusion, arts and music should be compulsory in schools to a large extent, because they develop creativity and give all pupils access, provided that the time is reasonable and choice is offered.

Ví dụ học sinh nhút nhát vào dàn hợp xướng của trường phát hiện tài năng và tự tin mà giờ toán không cho. 235.text:
Debates about whether art or science matters more are old, and some believe that art is more important than science. I disagree with this view to a large extent, since both meet essential human needs, and in terms of material survival, science is more important.

To begin with, science meets basic needs on which everything else depends. Science improves health, safety and living standards: vaccines, clean water, agriculture, energy and communications all result from scientific research. Without medicine, many people would die young, and without technology, modern life would be impossible. People who are hungry or ill cannot enjoy art, so material needs have to be met first. In emergencies such as pandemics or natural disasters, society looks to scientists for solutions, not to artists. Scientific method also teaches rational thinking, which protects people from superstition and misinformation.

However, art is also essential in a different way. Art gives meaning, beauty and shared identity and shapes how people understand their lives. Music, literature and painting express emotions, record history and help people through difficult times, and many societies judge their achievements by their culture as much as by their wealth. An engineer who designs a bridge, for example, needs science to make it strong and art to make it beautiful. Art and science also depend on each other, since scientific discoveries are sparked by imagination and artists use new technology. To claim that one is more important than the other is therefore a false choice. A society needs both, though science has the stronger claim when it comes to survival.

In conclusion, I disagree that art is more important than science, because science meets basic needs, although art gives life meaning and the two should be valued together.

387.text:
Every city faces a choice between preserving old buildings and replacing them with something new, and some people believe that restoring historic buildings is more important than building new structures. Others disagree. This essay will consider both perspectives before explaining my own opinion.

On the one hand, supporters of restoration argue that old buildings carry memory and identity. Historic buildings tell the story of a community, attract tourists and often have a quality of craftsmanship that is expensive to reproduce. Once demolished, they cannot be replaced, and a city that replaces all its old streets with modern blocks loses its character. Restoration also tends to be more sustainable, since reusing a building saves the energy and materials needed for new construction. An old factory converted into flats and studios, for example, gives new life to a building while keeping the character of the district. Preserving buildings also helps local people to feel proud and connected to their area.

On the other hand, supporters of new building point out that societies have modern needs. Cities need homes, offices, schools and hospitals, and old buildings can be costly to heat, repair and adapt to modern safety standards. In a growing city, refusing to build new structures can raise housing costs and leave people living in poor conditions. New buildings can also be designed to be energy efficient, accessible and attractive, and they will become the heritage of future generations. Rigid protection of every old building can therefore hold a city back.

In conclusion, both views have merit. Personally, I believe that important and irreplaceable buildings should be restored, while ordinary ones can be adapted or replaced, and that the best solution is often to reuse historic buildings for modern purposes.

analysis.type_vi: Discuss both views: phục hồi toà nhà lịch sử quan trọng hơn xây công trình mới

plan.think: Mở bài nêu lựa chọn của mọi thành phố (giữ toà nhà cũ hay thay mới) rồi hai phe; ý kiến riêng: phục hồi toà nhà quan trọng, không thể thay thế; toà nhà thường thì có thể thích nghi hoặc thay; tái sử dụng cho mục đích hiện đại.

Toà nhà cũ mang ký ức và bản sắc: kể câu chuyện cộng đồng, thu hút khách, thường có chất lượng thủ công đắt để tái tạo; phá rồi không thay được, thành phố thay hết phố cũ bằng khối hiện đại mất đặc trưng; phục hồi bền vững hơn vì tái sử dụng tiết kiệm năng lượng và vật liệu xây mới. Ví dụ nhà máy cũ chuyển thành căn hộ và xưởng nghệ sĩ giữ đặc trưng khu phố. Người địa phương tự hào, gắn với khu vực.

Xã hội có nhu cầu hiện đại: thành phố cần nhà, văn phòng, trường học, bệnh viện; toà nhà cũ tốn kém sưởi, sửa, nâng chuẩn an toàn; thành phố tăng trưởng từ chối xây mới có thể đẩy giá nhà, người sống điều kiện kém; công trình mới có thể thiết kế tiết kiệm năng lượng, dễ tiếp cận, đẹp, sẽ thành di sản của thế hệ sau; bảo vệ cứng nhắc mọi toà nhà cũ kìm hãm thành phố.
Phục hồi toà nhà quan trọng, thích nghi hoặc thay toà nhà thường, thường tốt nhất là tái sử dụng.
